brief.headline: Mohammed fell at home on Nov 3 about 10 days after starting apixaban for new atrial fibrillation, and he has lost 6.5% of his body weight since Sep 5 while his caregiver reports exhaustion.

items.statement: Fall in the kitchen on 2026-11-03 while reaching for a cabinet. He was found on the floor by his grandson Linda. He denied head strike or loss of consciousness, and no injury was noted. Fall risk was reassessed as high and a PT referral was placed. This fall came 10 days after apixaban was started on 2026-10-24.
items.verifier_note: The nursing note supports the fall details, high fall risk and PT referral. The medication record and PCP note give an apixaban start of 10-24, which is 10 days before 11-03.

items.statement: Weight fell from 92.0 kg on 2026-09-05 to 86.0 kg on 2026-11-24 (-6.0 kg, -6.5%). Readings were 89.9 kg on 10-01 and 87.8 kg on 10-28. He reports poor appetite, skips breakfast, and eats about 50% of day center lunches. Dietitian plan: oral supplement twice daily, weekly weights, dental check for chewing problems.
items.verifier_note: The vitals record has all four weights and the -6.0 kg (-6.5%) change. The dietitian note supports the appetite, breakfast, 50% lunch intake and plan details.

items.statement: On 2026-10-13 his grandson and primary caregiver Linda reported exhaustion and poor sleep, said she is worried about managing evenings alone, and requested respite. Respite options and a caregiver support group were discussed. The notes do not show whether respite has been arranged. Linda also found him after the Nov 3 fall.
items.verifier_note: The social work note supports Linda's report, the respite request and the options discussed. The nursing note supports Linda finding him after the fall. Nothing in the cited notes shows respite was arranged.

items.statement: PT evaluation on 2026-11-08 found slow, unsteady gait with intermittent cane use and a Timed Up and Go of 19 seconds. PT recommends a front-wheeled walker, a home safety evaluation, and bathroom grab bars. PT will see him twice weekly for strength and balance.
items.verifier_note: Every detail matches the PT evaluation note: gait, cane use, TUG of 19 seconds, the three recommendations and twice-weekly visits.

items.statement: Apixaban 5 mg was started on 2026-10-24 for new atrial fibrillation found on ECG. The pharmacist reconciled it on 10-26, checked interactions, and updated the blister pack. The active list still shows aspirin, clopidogrel and prasugrel alongside apixaban. It also shows two metoprolol formulations (succinate and tartrate) and two statins (lovastatin and simvastatin).
items.verifier_note: The apixaban start, indication, 10-26 pharmacist reconciliation, interaction check and blister pack update are supported. The cited sources do not show an active list with aspirin, clopidogrel, prasugrel, two metoprolol formulations or two statins.

items.statement: The PCP planned a recheck 4 weeks after starting apixaban, which falls around 2026-11-21. The PCP note of 11-16 says chronic conditions are stable, and no note in the evidence documents the apixaban recheck.
items.verifier_note: The PCP note says to recheck in 4 weeks, which is about 11-21. The 11-16 PCP note says chronic conditions are stable and does not mention an apixaban recheck.

questions_for_team: With the Nov 3 fall and unsteady gait, how should the team review fall and bleeding risk on apixaban? Does the PCP want to look at the active list of aspirin, clopidogrel, prasugrel and apixaban together?
Do the duplicate metoprolol and statin entries on the active medication list reflect what he actually takes? Can the pharmacist confirm?
Was the 4-week apixaban recheck done? If not, who will schedule it?
What is driving the weight loss (appetite, chewing, mood, other)? Who will follow the weekly weights and the dental check?
Can respite and evening support for Linda be arranged soon? Can the walker, home safety evaluation and grab bars be completed at the same time?

checks: Atrial fibrillation: confirm the ECG finding date, rate/rhythm documentation, and who ordered and reviewed it; check for any follow-up cardiology or EP visit since the apixaban start on 2026-10-24.

Anticoagulation safety: review the apixaban start, dosing against age/weight/renal function, and any bleeding events (GI, urinary, nasal from chronic sinusitis, bruising, Hgb trend given known anemia). Confirm the team has documented the rationale for combining with antiplatelet therapy.

Antiplatelet and statin duplication: flag concurrent aspirin, clopidogrel AND prasugrel (three P2Y12/antiplatelet agents listed as active) plus two statins (lovastatin and simvastatin) plus two beta-blocker entries (metoprolol succinate and metoprolol tartrate). Verify with the prescriber and pharmacy which are actually being taken, and whether any were stopped or should have been discontinued in the window.

Medication starts and stops since 2026-09-01: reconcile the active list against the pharmacy fill history and the EHR discontinuation log; note any new prescriptions, dose changes, or stops in the window.
Falls, ED visits, and admissions in the window: specifically check for fall or bleeding-related presentations, chest pain or cardiac admissions, and any post-discharge follow-up gaps.
Cardiac status: review chest pain or nitroglycerin use, dyspnea, palpitations, and any cardiology visits, given history of NSTEMI (2007) and ischemic heart disease (2018).
Blood pressure and heart rate trend over the window, including orthostatic readings if available, given hypertension and dual beta-blocker entries.

Labs: renal function and CBC (hemoglobin/platelets) for apixaban and antiplatelet monitoring; lipid panel and glucose/HbA1c given hyperlipidemia, metabolic syndrome, and prediabetes; check whether any labs are overdue.
Weight and BMI trend, since obesity and metabolic syndrome are active; check for dietary or activity goals in the care plan.

Function, cognition, mood, and caregiver: ADL/IADL changes, cognitive screen status, depression screen, PACE attendance and missed day-center or transport visits, and caregiver strain or availability since the last review on 2026-11-30 cycle; confirm care-plan items due in the window (assessments, reassessments, goal updates).
